family.description: This is a family of integral membrane proteins where the alignment appears to contain two duplicated modules of three transmembrane helices. The proteins are involved in the transport of anions across the cytoplasmic membrane [[cite:PUB00060436]] during taurine metabolism as an exporter of sulfoacetate [[cite:PUB00060437]]. This family used to be known as DUF81.

record.description: This is a family of integral membrane proteins where the alignment appears to contain two duplicated modules of three transmembrane helices. The proteins are involved in the transport of anions across the cytoplasmic membrane [[cite:PUB00060436]] during taurine metabolism as an exporter of sulfoacetate [[cite:PUB00060437]]. This family used to be known as DUF81.

evidence.explanation: CysZ sulfate uptake is a hypothesis based on conditional growth and rescue; direct flux and affinity were not measured.
MamO affects processing in cells; tested protease-region mutations lie outside PF01925 and depend on the LimO background.
PmpC affects normalized pigment; exported substrate z and the coexpression mechanism remain unknown.

discussions.notes: Current reference intervals are MamO357-633,CysZ7-246,PmpC5-260. Deposited CysZ/PmpC sequences match current accessions; exact historical plasmids/deletions remain qualified. Retain CysZ pEC-XK99E/pZ8-1 discrepancy, inaccessible primer supplement, unmatched WT/mutant sulfate doses and nested replication. Retain PmpC abundance/localization gaps and printed antibiotic units. MamO metal binding belongs to the separate N-terminal construct, not PF01925. The 2011 protease interpretation is not adopted over the 2016 pseudoprotease evidence.
discussions.prompt: Resolve biochemical transport mechanisms without transferring annotation or whole-protein phenotypes to the Pfam domain.
discussions.rationale: Gene-level growth, processing and pigment effects do not establish substrate identity, transport direction, coupling or isolated-domain sufficiency.

evidence.explanation: H16_B1872 transcription and pathway context motivate sulfite export; they are not TauE flux measurements.
SafE1/2 are transcriptionally supported candidates, distinct from measured SafD chemistry.
JMP134 delta-tauE has no detectable sulfide-oxidation/sulfate-output defect in the tested resting-cell context.

discussions.notes: Do not transfer TsaT reconstituted channel activity to TsaS, or Oenococcus plasmid prevalence to TauE-specific fitness or transport. The JMP134 negative does not prove absent function across species. Follow-ups include MSR-1 MamO truncations, RS-1 genetics, later MamO/MamE studies, H16 alternative sulfonates, IsfE, BigR-linked systems, keratin pathways and eukaryotic/archaeal members. Source and access ledger: evidence/PF01925/coverage.txt. This is same-agent partial scientific curation, not exhaustive family coverage, independent endorsement or publication.
discussions.prompt: Extend remaining experimental contexts and keep proposed transport assignments separate from demonstrated flux.
